text:
maria: Heads up — EU1 dedicated pool is saturated, seeing p95/p99 latency spikes for a chunk of tenants (2x-5x). Started ~07:12 UTC. Kernel selection logs show a lot of fallbacks to the fp32 path. Tagging @eng-runtime and @oncall. :warning:

oncall: I'm on it, pulling metrics and flamegraphs now. Any recent config changes?

alex: Grafana -> https://console.redwood/eu1/dedicated/pools shows GPU util at 96%, scheduler queue length spiked, and p99 generation latency jumped 120ms -> ~1.1s for affected tenants.

chris: pulling runtime logs, lots of lines like:
```
[07:11:58] kernel_selector: model=llama-13b-v2 variant=q4_0 selected_kernel=unsupported_quant -> fallback=fp32_slow_path
[07:12:01] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.78 host=gpu-42 tenant=tenant-123
[07:12:03] batcher: created_small_batches=235 large_batches=12 avg_wait_ms=9
```
seems the selector decided fallback because quant profile didn't match sequence length distribution.

maria: timeline matches. We also saw scheduling decisions put 7 big tenants onto the same rack yesterday during a placement change. tim any input?

tim: yes — yesterday infra rolled a placement tweak to reduce cross-rack traffic and we temporarily disabled tenant spread for the eu1-dedicated pool (patch 7c2b) to improve allocation speed. That accidentally concentrated hot tenants.

alex: so noisy neighbor (hot tenant concentration) + kernel selector choosing slower path + KV cache thrash = multiplicative latency. I deployed a quick profiler trace on gpu-42. Here's a sampled stack (hot path):
```
serve_infer -> dispatch_kernels -> fp32_attention_kernel -> memcopy -> stall_wait_for_io
```

devops-bot: Incident created: INC-202203-eu1-saturation. Pagerduty alerted 07:14 UTC.

eva: KV metrics show TTL churn — many tenants evicting and refilling KV cache due to bursty seq lengths. Cache occupancy for gpu-42 dropped to 28% at spike. Increasing TTL should help.

chris: quick mitigation proposal:
- revert placement change (re-enable tenant spread) to avoid hot concentration
- revert kernel-selector patch that changed fallback thresholds (PR #4598)
- bump KV cache TTL for affected pool to 60s
- temporarily increase pool capacity (scale +2 nodes) for 20m to absorb backlog

oncall: I can execute placement revert and scale up now. Who can revert the kernel selector PR?

alex: I can. Pushing rollback PR and will monitor.

maria: I'm applying KV TTL bump to eu1-dedicated (config path: /configs/dedicated/eu1/cache/kv_ttl_s). Command:
```bash
redwoodctl set-config eu1 dedicated kv_ttl_s=60 --reason "incident: reduce evictions"
```

tim: re-enabled tenant spread (rolled back patch 7c2b) and kicked the scheduler to rebalance. That should start migrating hot tenants away from gpu-42.

chris: kernel rollback merged at 07:22 UTC (r4571 -> r4569). Early traces show kernel selector back to previous thresholds.

alex: scaled pool +2 nodes at 07:23 UTC. New capacity online by ~07:26 UTC. Backpressure in queues dropped, p99 falling.

maria: monitoring now — p95 back to baseline, p99 trending down from 1.1s -> ~220ms over last 7 minutes. KV occupancy rising.

oncall: customers with SLA risk identified: tenant-123, tenant-77, tenant-99. Ops notified via email template.

eva: adding one more tweak: disable aggressive prefix caching for the three hottest tenants to avoid small-batch pathological behavior for now.

alex: confirming: no code-level regressions besides the kernel selector change. We should run the selector A/B test in staging with longer sequence tails.

maria: incident summary for runbook:
- root cause: hot-tenant concentration due to placement config change + kernel selector thresholds leading to fallback to slower fp32 path + KV cache thrash causing repeated recomputation
- impact: EU1 dedicated pool p99 latency spike, partial SLA risk for 3 tenants, throughput drop while queues backlogged
- mitigations performed: reverted placement patch; rolled back kernel-selector PR; increased KV TTL to 60s; scaled pool +2 nodes; disabled aggressive prefix caching on hottest tenants; notified customers
- follow-ups: automated test for kernel selector with long-tail seq distributions; add placement policy alert when >X% load on single rack; re-evaluate default KV TTL and caching heuristics; post-incident perf profiling to tune batching heuristics

chris: I'll own the postmortem doc and perf regression ticket. alex/eva/tim please add any config diffs to the ticket.

maria: great work team. Closing the pager and monitoring for 1h before marking resolved. :thumbsup:
